image_description: A wooden staircase interior featuring a prominent bannister system. The handrail is dark polished wood with a curved profile, supported by slender vertical balusters. A large newel post anchors the bottom left corner. The stairs have yellow painted risers and wooden treads. In the background, there is a white door frame and wall.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A continuous dark wood handrail is visible, supported by multiple vertical balusters that appear evenly spaced along the incline.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The white trim around the background opening appears geometrically inconsistent. The vertical jamb seems to merge or bleed into the horizontal header without a sharp corner, and the perspective lines do not converge logically with the rest of the room.
The yellow paint on the risers lacks realistic surface variation or brush strokes, appearing as flat, noisy color blocks rather than painted wood or drywall.
The end of the handrail at the top right seems to fade or terminate abruptly without a clear connection to a wall or newel post, defying standard construction logic.

Geometric logic of the background doorway/frame.
